title: Migration runner for the e-commerce schema
name: Schema migration runner

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this runner keeps the schema and its migration history consistent, including when a process dies mid-run? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two instances boot simultaneously and both call upgrade(). Why can they not both run migration 2?
choices: The primary key on schema_migrations.version rejects the second record, which aborts its migration.
Each migration is wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT, and PostgreSQL serializes concurrent transactions touching the same table.
pg_advisory_lock blocks the second instance on the same session-level lock until the first has released it, and the applied set is read only after acquiring it.
The connection pool hands out a single connection at a time, so upgrade() calls never overlap.

questions.prompt: In migration 2, the UPDATE succeeds but SET NOT NULL fails because another process inserted an order with a NULL warehouse_id in between. What state does the database end up in for that migration's changes?
choices: The warehouse_id column does not exist, as the statements ran in one transaction and were rolled back together.
The warehouse_id column exists with the backfilled values, but is still nullable.
The column exists and is NOT NULL, since the UPDATE already removed all NULLs.
The column exists, and the runner retries the failing statement until it succeeds.

questions.prompt: The migration process is killed while the advisory lock is held, in the middle of a statement inside BEGIN. What can be said about the lock and the half-run statements?
choices: The lock stays held until an operator calls pg_advisory_unlock, because the finally block never ran.
The statements are committed because the connection is in autocommit mode.
Nothing is rolled back; the server waits for the client to reconnect and continue the transaction.
The server releases the session-level lock when the connection closes and rolls back the open transaction, so other instances can proceed.
